claims.claim: arXiv authors published on 2026-10-11
a fully automatic approach to weak-to-strong verifier hardening
agent environments use programmatic verifiers to turn complex outcomes into rewards
verifiers can be attacked into awarding full credit to cheating agents without completing the intended task
the method first sets up an isolated verifier sandbox that agents cannot directly modify
then runs a hacker-fixer loop to find and repair remaining verifier vulnerabilities
Applied to Terminal Bench, KernelBench, and SETA, it substantially reduced attack success
the iterative design outperformed the static, non-iterative baseline
An earlier version of the loop has been adopted by the official Terminal Bench repository to audit exploits
MAI-Gym's authors released the platform on 2026-10-14
an open all-in-one system unifying GUI agent evaluation, data collection, and online RL training across mobile, computer, and web environments
A shared rollout pipeline keeps agent behavior consistent between evaluation and training
ten established benchmarks are supported
the platform scales to 20,000 parallel environment instances
The trained model, MAI-Gym-9B, reaches 78.4% on MobileWorld and 76.2% on OSWorld-Verified
state of the art among open GUI agents under 10B parameters
They also release the framework, synthesis skills, mocked apps, 2,000 verified tasks, and the model checkpoint
RL in a mocked train-ticketing app lifted real-phone success from 28.8% to 48.1%
online reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards has driven rapid progress in mathematics, coding, and tool use
scaling that success to GUI agents remains challenging because interactive environments cost too much and realistic training tasks are scarce
MAI-Gym enables automated synthesis of diverse GUI applications and challenging tasks, including resettable mocked apps and coherent cross-app worlds with execution-validated task verifiers

lifted_claims: MAI-Gym enables automated synthesis of diverse GUI applications and challenging tasks, including resettable mocked apps and coherent cross-app worlds with execution-validated task verifiers

claims.claim: GitHub announced on October 19, 2026 that it had deprecated a set of models across most Copilot experiences
including Copilot Chat, inline edits, ask and agent modes, and code completions
Workflows and integrations need updating to supported models
no action is required to remove the deprecated ones
Copilot Enterprise administrators may need to enable access to alternative models through their model policies in Copilot settings
then confirm the policy is enabled for the specific model
Once enabled, the model appears in the Copilot Chat model selector in VS Code and on github.com
Terminal-RSI's authors published on 2026-10-15
a method that alternates Recursive Self-Rewrite of verified trajectories with critic-inheriting Recursive Policy-Refine
A five-stage sequence from a Qwen3.8-27B base through RSR-1, RPR-1, RSR-2 and RPR-2 yields Terminal-RSI-27B
scoring 19.84% on Terminal-Bench 4.0
86.52% on Terminal-Bench 2.1
16.95% on Terminal-Bench 3.0
79.00% on Terminal-Bench Hard
On LHTB, process reward rises from 0.21 to 0.37
strict completion from 0/46 to 5/46
SWR100 success from 3.00% to 6.00%
Family Dense Reward calibrates semantic progress across task families
GitHub made agentic autofix for code scanning alerts generally available for Code Security and Advanced Security customers on GitHub Enterprise Cloud
